climate.overview_html: Three major UN climate reports in eight days set the starkest pre-COP31 scientific record in the summit’s history. The WMO’s 22nd Greenhouse Gas Bulletin, released October 27 — twelve days before COP31 opens in Antalya — confirmed that atmospheric CO₂ averaged 426.8 ppm in 2025, a record 153% of pre-industrial levels and the highest concentration in at least 800,000 years of ice-core records. UNEP’s Emissions Gap Report 2026 The Point of Return (October 21) concluded that staying within 1.5°C without overshoot is no longer possible; current policies put warming at 2.8°C this century while full delivery of all NDCs would reach only 2.6°C. Meanwhile, China has signalled it will formally raise clean-tech tariffs as a COP31 agenda item, with Vice Minister Li Gao framing Western trade barriers as a “new problem” that undermines global climate action — adding a trade flashpoint to an agenda the Turkish presidency has not named coal, oil or gas at all.

items.headline: WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin No. 22: CO₂ Hits 426.8 ppm in 2025 — Record 153% of Pre-Industrial; CH₄ and N₂O Also at All-Time Highs; Growth Rate Tripled Since 1960s; COP31 Twelve Days Away
items.summary: The WMO's 22nd annual Greenhouse Gas Bulletin, released October 27, twelve days before COP31 opens, reports that CO₂ reached a global average of 426.8 ppm in 2025 — a record 153% of the 1750 pre-industrial baseline and the highest concentration measured in at least 800,000 years of ice-core records. Methane and nitrous oxide also set records. CO₂ growth rates have tripled since the 1960s; the 2024–2025 increase of 2.8 ppm is above the decadal average, partly amplified by the current El Niño driving land-carbon-flux anomalies. WMO expects further concentration rises in 2026. The document is specifically timed to provide authoritative science for COP31 negotiators in Antalya.

items.headline: UNEP Emissions Gap Report 2026 “The Point of Return”: 1.5°C Overshoot Now Inevitable; Current Policies = 2.8°C; Full NDC Delivery = 2.6°C; Emissions Must Fall 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035, 69% by 2040
items.summary: UNEP's Emissions Gap Report 2026, titled 'The Point of Return' and released October 21, finds that keeping warming below 1.5°C without overshoot is no longer achievable. Under current policies, warming could reach 2.8°C this century. Even if all national pledges were fully delivered including conditional targets, warming would still land near 2.6°C. To return to a below-1.5°C pathway by 2100, emissions must fall roughly 18% by 2030, 45% by 2035 and 69% by 2040 relative to 2025. Time summarised the report under 'Five Facts You Need To Know' and it is considered the key scientific reference for Antalya negotiations.

items.source: Climate Change News / Reuters / The Standard HK
items.headline: COP31 Trade Flashpoint: China to Formally Push Back on Clean-Tech Tariffs at Antalya; Vice Minister Li Gao Calls US/EU Protectionism a “New Problem” Threatening Collective Climate Action; Free Flow of Green Technology on Beijing’s Agenda
items.summary: China signalled on October 22 that it will push to include cleantech trade barriers as a formal topic at COP31, with Vice Minister Li Gao framing US and EU tariffs on Chinese solar, EVs and wind turbines as a 'new problem' threatening global collective climate action. Li said China would 'respond firmly to attacks' and called for the free flow of green technology as part of the Antalya agenda. China dominates global production of solar panels, wind turbines, batteries and EVs; the US has imposed steep tariffs on Chinese solar and clean vehicles while the EU has done the same for autos. The COP31 presidency's published agenda does not mention coal, oil or gas phase-out, and Climate Change News reports broader developing-country pressure to include finance, technology transfer and trade alongside emissions ambition.

major_events.name: Cyclone Arnab — Landfall COMPLETE 28 Oct ~1:20 a.m. IST near Bapatla–Machilipatnam; System Now Inland Weakening; 2 Deaths Confirmed; 570,000 Had Evacuated
major_events.status: As of 28 Oct morning: The IMD confirmed landfall around 1:20 a.m. IST near Bapatla–Machilipatnam at 125–135 km/h sustained winds and gusts to 150 km/h; the system has moved inland and is weakening from Very Severe Cyclonic Storm status. At least 2 people have been killed by electrocution as gusts downed trees and power poles across East Godavari, Kakinada and Machilipatnam districts. Waterlogging is reported across Kakinada town. School closures in parts of Jharkhand and Odisha are extended through October 29. The system is expected to dissipate within 24–48 hours.
major_events.impact: Andhra Pradesh: 2 deaths confirmed (electrocution); trees and power poles downed; waterlogging Kakinada; landfall complete ~1:20am IST Oct 28 at 125–135 km/h gusts 150 km/h. Odisha/Jharkhand: heavy rain, school closures through Oct 29. System: now weakening inland, expected to dissipate within 24–48h. 570,000 had been evacuated pre-landfall.

major_events.name: Typhoon In-fa (JTWC 30W) — Intensifying toward Super Typhoon; 220–240 km/h Forecast Peak; Near-Stall ~1,500 km East of Saipan; Track toward Pagan/CNMI Oct 30–31
major_events.status: As of 28 Oct: Typhoon In-fa has nearly stalled approximately 1,500 km east of Saipan while holding Category 4 intensity; JTWC’s latest advisory forecasts sustained winds of 130 knots (~150 mph) by Thursday morning, meeting the super typhoon threshold. RNZ and Zoom Earth tracking place current intensity at 220 km/h with a peak forecast of 240 km/h before landfall. The forecast track places the center near or over Pagan Island, CNMI around late Friday October 30. Guam NWS says Guam itself remains outside the current forecast cone but track uncertainty remains high; no typhoon watch or warning is yet in effect for Guam or the CNMI as of Oct 28 morning.
major_events.impact: CNMI/Pagan: direct impact expected Oct 30–31 at potentially Cat 4–5 intensity; large dangerous swells already building. Saipan: southern edge of cone, preparations for worst-case scenario advised. Guam: outside current cone, monitoring. No watches/warnings yet as of Oct 28 morning.

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia/Borneo/Sumatra) — Hotspots Fall to 93; Underground Fires Persist Despite Rain; 333,470 Respiratory Cases; Jakarta Protests Continue
major_events.status: As of 27 Oct: Indonesia’s Forestry Ministry reported high-confidence fire hotspots dropped to 93 — down from 147 the previous day — as rainfall reached several affected provinces. However, Malay Mail reports underground peat fires continue to smoulder because oxygen in the drained peat column sustains combustion below the surface despite surface rainfall; 61 aircraft remain deployed. TechTimes cites WMO warnings that the 2026 haze may be the worst transboundary pollution event on record in Southeast Asia, with 333,470 confirmed respiratory illness cases across seven provinces. Jakarta protests demanding a national disaster declaration continue.
major_events.impact: Indonesia: 333,470+ respiratory illness cases (7 provinces); ~1.9M hectares burned; hotspots at 93 (down from 147); 61 aircraft deployed; underground fires resistant to rainfall. Malaysia/Singapore: ongoing unhealthy air quality. ~40 million people exposed. Monsoon onset not expected until late October/November.

weather.overview_html: Cyclone Arnab completed landfall near Bapatla–Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh in the early hours of October 28, killing at least 2 people and downing trees and power infrastructure across Kakinada, East Godavari and Machilipatnam — ending a three-day evacuation that moved 570,000 residents. The system is now weakening inland and expected to dissipate within 48 hours. Typhoon In-fa meanwhile remains nearly stationary ~1,500 km east of Saipan, intensifying toward super typhoon status before its forecast track toward Pagan Island, CNMI, around October 30–31. In Southeast Asia, Indonesia’s hotspot count fell to 93 on October 27 as rain reached affected provinces, though underground peat fires continue to resist surface water and 61 aircraft remain deployed.

items.headline: Cyclone Arnab Landfall Complete near Bapatla–Machilipatnam at 1:20 a.m. IST; 125–135 km/h Sustained Winds, Gusts 150 km/h; 2 Killed by Electrocution; Waterlogging Kakinada; System Now Weakening Inland
items.summary: IMD confirmed Cyclone Arnab made landfall near Bapatla–Machilipatnam, Andhra Pradesh, starting around 1:20 a.m. IST on October 28 at Very Severe Cyclonic Storm intensity: 125–135 km/h sustained winds with gusts to 150 km/h. The system moved inland and began weakening immediately after landfall. At least two people were killed by electrocution as gusts downed power lines and trees across East Godavari, Kakinada and Machilipatnam; waterlogging was reported in Kakinada town. The AP government had evacuated 570,000 residents prior to landfall; 10 NDRF and 11 SDRF teams were deployed. Schools in parts of Jharkhand remain closed through October 29. The system is expected to dissipate within 24–48 hours.

items.headline: Indonesia Peatland Fires: Hotspots Fall to 93 (Down from 147); Underground Peat Burns Persist Despite Rain; 61 Aircraft Still Deployed; 333,470 Respiratory Cases; WMO Warns Worst Transboundary Haze Event on Record
items.summary: Indonesia's Forestry Ministry reported on October 27 that high-confidence fire hotspots fell to 93 nationwide, down from 147 the previous day, as rainfall reached several fire-affected provinces in Borneo and Sumatra. However, underground peat fires continue to resist surface rainfall because oxygen in the drained peat column sustains subsurface smouldering — a structural challenge that cannot be solved by precipitation alone. The ministry said 61 aircraft remain deployed for water bombing and weather modification; patrols, ember searches and mop-up continue until all conditions are confirmed safe. TechTimes cited WMO warnings that the 2026 haze event may be the worst transboundary pollution event on record in Southeast Asia, with 333,470 confirmed respiratory illness cases across seven provinces. Jakarta protests demanding a national disaster declaration continue.

renewables.overview_html: Africa’s largest solar-plus-storage project has broken ground: Infinity Power and HAU Energy commenced full construction on Egypt’s Nefer Minya project — 1.2 GWp of solar paired with 600 MWh of battery storage — backed by a $566 million debt financing package. On storage fundamentals, India’s Central Electricity Authority logged 5.3 GWh of operational grid-scale BESS with 185 GWh more in the confirmed pipeline — the country’s most ambitious storage backlog on record — while Greece added 2.7 GW of new renewable capacity in the first ten months of 2026, pushing total installed capacity to ~19 GW. Germany’s regulator meanwhile opened a tender for 2,226 MW of new ground-mounted solar with bids due December 1, one of the largest single solar auctions since Germany’s 2024 framework reform.

items.headline: Egypt’s Nefer Minya 1.2 GWp Solar + 600 MWh Battery Project Enters Full Construction; $566 Million Debt Financing Secured; Infinity Power and HAU Energy Build Africa’s Largest Solar-Storage Project
items.summary: Infinity Power (a Masdar/Infinity joint venture) and HAU Energy have begun full construction on Egypt's Nefer Minya solar-plus-storage project. The project pairs 1.2 GWp of utility-scale solar PV with 600 MWh of co-located battery storage and was enabled by a $566 million debt financing package. Nefer Minya is one of the largest single clean-energy projects in Africa. It will supply power to Egypt's national grid to address the country's electricity shortfall and meet the government's 42%-renewable-by-2030 target.

items.headline: India Battery Storage: 5.3 GWh Operational, 185 GWh in Pipeline — Largest-Ever Announced BESS Backlog as Grid-Scale Procurement Accelerates Toward 60 GWh 2030 Target
items.summary: India's Central Electricity Authority (CEA) figures, reported October 28, show approximately 5.3 GWh of grid-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) currently operational nationwide, with a further 185 GWh in the confirmed project pipeline. The pipeline is the country's largest-ever announced battery storage backlog, driven by India's Viability Gap Funding scheme and accelerating DISCOM procurement tenders. India's national energy storage target is 60 GWh by 2030 under the National Electricity Plan; the 185 GWh pipeline represents more than three times that target, signalling a substantial oversubscription of ambition vs the current policy floor.

items.headline: Greece Adds 2.7 GW New Renewables in First 10 Months of 2026, Reaching ~19 GW Total Installed; Solar PV Accounts for Majority; Record Monthly Additions in September
items.summary: Greece connected approximately 2.7 GW of new renewable energy capacity in the first ten months of 2026, predominantly solar PV, bringing total installed renewable capacity to approximately 19 GW. September saw record monthly additions. The expansion reflects rapid progress under Greece's national energy and climate plan targeting 70% renewable electricity by 2030 and has contributed to a significant reduction in dependence on natural gas and lignite, putting Greece ahead of several northern European countries in per-capita renewable deployment rate.

items.headline: Germany Opens 2,226 MW Ground-Mounted Solar Tender; Bids Due December 1, 2026; One of the Largest Single Solar Auction Rounds Since 2024 Framework Reform
items.summary: Germany's Federal Network Agency (Bundesnetzagentur) opened a tender for approximately 2,226 MW of new ground-mounted solar PV capacity with a bid deadline of December 1, 2026. The tender is one of the largest single solar auction rounds since Germany reformed its auction framework in 2024. Results are expected in early 2027. The round reflects the government's accelerated Energiewende targets as Germany seeks to offset coal closures and fill the gap left by nuclear phase-out, and follows September's record-high solar generation output for the country.

science.overview_html: Three arXiv papers this cycle push the AI weather-to-climate frontier in new directions. arXiv:2610.28973, accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning workshop, demonstrates for the first time that weather foundation models can quantify carbon dioxide removal uncertainty from enhanced weathering at operational scale — directly bridging the AI weather-forecasting and carbon-removal communities. arXiv:2610.22555 embeds an AI foundation model in the UK’s UKCA atmospheric chemistry framework, achieving stable 50-year autoregressive runs of full chemistry, aerosol and radiation fields at ~100× the speed of the host physics-based model. Beucler, Neelin and twelve co-authors (arXiv:2610.09770) lay out a minimal testable framework for trustworthy AI climate modeling: explicit external forcings, physically constrained state tendencies, and mandatory out-of-distribution stress testing in extremes and counterfactual scenarios. The NPR investigation into Google DeepMind’s Isaias track call continues to circulate widely among operational forecasters.

items.headline: How AI Is Transforming Hurricane Forecasts: Google DeepMind Called Isaias’s Florida Panhandle Landfall When NHC Was Tracking Southeast Louisiana; But AI Lagged 20–40% on Intensity; Forecasters Uneasy with “Black Box” Guidance
items.summary: NPR's October 26 investigation found that Google DeepMind's AI model predicted Hurricane Isaias would make landfall on the Florida Panhandle early and correctly, while conventional NHC guidance initially placed the storm on a track toward southeastern Louisiana. The AI model showed 20–40% less skill than the NHC on intensity forecasting. The NHC began incorporating DeepMind's model into official guidance in 2025, where it quickly ranked among the top track predictors. Forecasters' key concern: they cannot diagnose why the model is right or wrong in any specific case, limiting diagnostic confidence. The model also failed on Hurricane Simon in the eastern Pacific.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.28973 — From Weather to Enhanced Weathering: Weather Foundation Models for Carbon Dioxide Removal at Operational Scale; Accepted NeurIPS 2026 Tackling Climate Change with ML Workshop
items.summary: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Tackling Climate Change with Machine Learning workshop, this paper applies weather foundation models to enhanced weathering operations — the spreading of crushed silicate rock on agricultural soils to accelerate CO₂ drawdown. The work quantifies CDR uncertainty at operational scale by propagating probabilistic output from AI weather models through the weathering-rate and carbon-flux calculation chain. It is the first paper to explicitly bridge the AI weather-forecasting and carbon-removal communities, arguing that weather-model uncertainty propagation should become a standard component of any MRV framework for CDR methods that depend on meteorological drivers.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.22555 — Atmospheric Chemistry–Climate Modeling with an AI Foundation Model: 50-Year Stable Autoregressive Simulation of Chemistry, Aerosol and Radiation at ~100× UKCA Speed
items.summary: This paper embeds an AI foundation model in the UK Chemistry and Aerosols (UKCA) framework to simulate daily meteorology, atmospheric composition, aerosol fields and radiation simultaneously. The key result: the model runs stably in autoregressive simulation for 50 years at approximately 100× the speed of the host UKCA physics-based chemistry model, making century-scale climate chemistry projections at high temporal frequency computationally feasible for the first time. The work extends AI atmospheric models (previously focused on dynamics alone) to full composition and chemistry cycles, with implications for air quality projection, radiative forcing assessment and climate sensitivity studies.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.09770 — Beucler, Neelin et al.: “AI Pathways from Weather to Climate” — Minimal Framework for Trustworthy AI Climate Modeling: Explicit Forcings, Physical Constraints, Out-of-Distribution Stress Tests Required
items.meta: arXiv:2610.09770 · T. Beucler (UNIL), D. Neelin (UCLA) + 12 authors · physics.ao-ph
items.summary: Beucler, Neelin and 12 co-authors (including Bretherton, Schneider, Zanna and Grover) argue that deep learning now emulates atmospheric reanalyses with sufficient fidelity to support well-calibrated ensemble weather forecasts, but bridging to climate timescales requires two additional properties: external forcings (GHGs, land use) must be represented explicitly and constrained to physically appropriate state tendencies, and models must be stress-tested in out-of-distribution regimes including extremes and counterfactual scenarios. The paper challenges the narrative that AI models are inherently more computationally efficient than GPU-ported dynamical models, but argues AI can deliver unique value by predicting target variables directly without integrating the full high-frequency multivariate state. ML downscaling can partially substitute for explicit fine-scale resolution where observations are available, enabling inexpensive local risk assessment across prediction horizons.

items.title: Rhizome Preparing US$15–20 M Series A for Grid-Resilience Climate-Risk AI Platform for Electric Utilities (Axios Pro Exclusive); Products Model How Extreme Weather and Long-Term Climate Shift Physical Grid Assets
items.body_html: Axios Pro Climate Deals reported October 19 that Rhizome — the software startup that models weather and climate risks for electric utilities — is preparing a Series A financing of US$15–20 million. The company’s platform (gridADAPT, gridFIRM, gridCAVA) combines AI with geospatial and historical outage data to quantify how extreme weather and long-term climate shifts affect grid infrastructure and where resilience spending delivers maximum return on investment. Rhizome has previously raised a $2.5 M seed (2023, Looking Glass/Intelis/CLAI) and a $6.5 M seed extension (May 2025). Target customers are investor-owned utilities and electric cooperatives navigating grid resilience requirements under FERC and state regulators.

items.title: CarbonFarm Closes €7 M (≈US$7.8 M) Series A for AI-Satellite MRV of Methane from Rice Farming; Led by Colam Impact; 19 Countries; Proparco, Bpifrance Among Participants
items.body_html: Paris-based CarbonFarm raised €7 million in a Series A led by Colam Impact, with Proparco, Suma Capital, elea, Working Capital Fund, Albo, Bpifrance and existing investors Serena and Techmind participating. CarbonFarm combines AI-powered satellite imagery, field-data collection tools and GHG modelling to quantify methane emissions at individual rice-field level, providing measurement, reporting and verification (MRV) data that can underpin carbon-credit issuance and corporate supply-chain decarbonisation commitments. The company now operates in 19 countries across Asia, Africa, Europe and Latin America. Rice paddy cultivation accounts for an estimated 10–12% of global anthropogenic methane emissions, making reliable field-level MRV a material gap in current carbon market infrastructure.

items.title: Reverion Raises US$175 M Series B for Carbon-Negative Reversible Solid Oxide Fuel Cell Power Plants; Led by Kembara; German Megafactory to 250 MW/yr Capacity; Claimed World-Record 74.2% Electrical Efficiency on Biogas
items.body_html: Reverion closed a US$175 million Series B led by Kembara, with Allianz, KfW Capital, Aurum Impact, Carbon Equity, Energy Impact Partners, UVC Partners and the European Innovation Council Fund among the participants. The company makes containerized solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems that convert biogas to electricity at a claimed 74.2% electrical efficiency without combustion, capturing CO₂ in pure form — yielding a carbon-negative balance on biogas. Units are reversible: surplus power runs them in electrolysis mode to produce hydrogen or synthetic methane. Proceeds fund a German megafactory targeting 250 MW/year manufacturing capacity (up ~10× from current). Seven units are already in live customer operation; pipeline value exceeds $2 billion.
items.source_html: ESG Today / Carbon Herald
